summary: Verified SisFall's real F01-F15/D01-D19 taxonomy against the primary source (Sucerquia et al. 2017, Sensors 17(1):198). SPARK's existing F01-F08/D01-D14 are reworded/reordered SisFall analogs, not verbatim copies — mapped each row to its SisFall counterpart. Drew F09-F15 (7 rows, clean match) and D15-D19 (5 rows) from SisFall's remaining un-mapped categories, adapted to SPARK's wrist coordinate frame and crash-mat safety rules. Flagged one exclusion (SisFall F07, table-assisted fall) on safety/feasibility grounds and one judgment call on 2 of the 5 ADL slots.
result_text:
### Research question
Does docs/DATA_COLLECTION_PROTOCOL.md's F09–F15 / D15–D19 gap match SisFall's actual published taxonomy, and what should the missing rows contain, consistent with §2.1 (safety) and §3.2 (coordinate frame)?

### Bottom line
SisFall's real taxonomy (Sucerquia et al. 2017, Sensors 17(1):198, DOI 10.3390/s17010198) is 15 fall types (F01–F15) and 19 ADL types (D01–D19), verified directly from the paper's Table 1/Table 2 (primary source, already in the main SPARK NLM notebook, source_id c4f5928e). SPARK's F01–F08 and D01–D14 are **not verbatim SisFall rows** — they are reworded/merged/reordered analogs (SPARK also adds wrist-specific ADLs like typing/writing/clapping that SisFall, a belt-worn device, never had). Mapping each existing SPARK row to its nearest SisFall category leaves exactly 7 SisFall fall types and (a judgment-weighted) 5 ADL types unused — a clean numeric match to the missing F09–F15/D15–D19 slots. Draft rows below fill that gap using SisFall's own content, adapted to SPARK's dorsal-wrist frame and mat/spotter safety rules.

### Key findings

**Finding 1 — SisFall's canonical taxonomy is confirmed and complete (Established).**
Evidence: Primary source Table 1 (falls) and Table 2 (ADLs), verbatim, retrieved from the notebook's indexed PDF of the published paper (Sensors 2017, 17, 198, p.4/14). 15 falls, 19 ADLs, 38 subjects (23 young adults 19–30y + 15 elderly 60–75y), 200 Hz, two accelerometers + one gyroscope, belt-buckle mounted.
Source: Sucerquia, López, Vargas-Bonilla (2017), Sensors 17(1):198, DOI 10.3390/s17010198.
Confidence: Established (primary source, verbatim table text with page citation).
Relevance to SPARK: This is the authoritative reference the protocol doc's "SisFall-compatible" claim (tracker v54, line 43) must be checked against — confirmed reliable to build on.

**Finding 2 — SPARK's F01–F08/D01–D14 are reworded analogs of SisFall, not copies (Established).**
Evidence: Row-by-row comparison (see table below) shows SPARK's descriptions/instructions differ in wording, merge multiple SisFall categories into one row (e.g. SPARK D03 "Jogging" merges SisFall D03+D04 slow/quick jogging), or add categories with no SisFall counterpart at all (D10 coughing/sneezing, D12 clapping/waving, D13 typing, D14 writing — plausible because SPARK is wrist-worn while SisFall is belt-worn, so wrist-specific arm motions matter that a waist sensor never captured).
Source: Direct diff of docs/DATA_COLLECTION_PROTOCOL.md §4.1/§4.2 vs. SisFall Table 1/Table 2.
Confidence: Established.
Relevance to SPARK: The doc cannot be "completed" by mechanically appending SisFall's own F09–F15/D15–D19 verbatim — each candidate row must first be checked against what SPARK has *already* covered under different wording, or duplicate mechanisms slip in.

**Finding 3 — Falls gap resolves cleanly: 7 unused SisFall fall types = 7 missing SPARK slots (Established / Supported inference on F07 exclusion).**
Evidence: Mapping SPARK F01→SisFall F04(trip-forward), F02→F01(slip-forward), F03→F02(slip-backward), F05/F06→F03(lateral slip, used twice for L/R), F07→F06(vertical/syncope), F08→F08(forward-get-up), F04→F11(backward-sit-miss) accounts for 7 of SisFall's 15 fall types (with F03 double-counted for laterality). That leaves 8 SisFall types unused (F05, F07, F09, F10, F12, F13, F14, F15) for exactly 7 open slots. SisFall's own paper explicitly excluded stair-falls from its 15 despite survey demand, citing injury risk ("not included here because of the high risk of having an accident" — Table 1 methodology text). F07 (fall while walking, catching a table, fainting) requires an unplanned furniture prop inside the crash-mat area not specified anywhere in §3 (Hardware Configuration) or §2.1 (Safety) — same injury-risk logic SisFall itself used to exclude stairs applies here. Excluding F07 leaves exactly 7 remaining types (F05, F09, F10, F12, F13, F14, F15) for the 7 open slots.
Source: SisFall Table 1 (primary); SPARK docs/DATA_COLLECTION_PROTOCOL.md §4.1, §2.1, §3.
Confidence: Established for the row-mapping; Supported inference for excluding F07 specifically (reasonable safety-parallel, not something the tracker states outright — flagged for Aaradhya to confirm no table prop is actually planned).
Relevance to SPARK: Gives a defensible, evidence-traceable fill for F09–F15 with no invented content and no duplication of F01–F08.

**Finding 4 — ADL gap is not a clean numeric match; 2 of 5 slots are a judgment call (Supported inference).**
Evidence: Mapping SPARK's D01–D14 to SisFall leaves D11 (sit-collapse-back-into-chair), D12 (lie down slowly), D13 (lie down quickly), D14 (supine-to-lateral), D16 (bend without knees), D17 (car entry/exit), D19 (gentle jump) unused — 7 candidates for 5 slots. D16, D17, D19 are strong, low-ambiguity picks: D16 tests a distinct trunk-flexion technique SPARK's existing D08 ("bending to pick up object," technique unspecified) doesn't isolate, and is specifically flagged in SisFall's own methodology as chosen because ADLs with waveforms similar to falls are the ones that generate false positives; D17 is a genuinely new category (and Nepal-relevant — public transport ingress/egress); D19 adds a vertical-acceleration spike distinct from SPARK's existing D09 (reach, no jump) and is directly relevant to Layer 1's |a|>2.5g hardware gate (R-01) as a false-positive stress test. The remaining 2 slots (recommended: D11, D12) are less clear-cut — D11 (near-fall/collapse-into-chair) is conceptually close to SPARK's existing D11-code "stumbling/near-fall recovery," and D12/D13/D14 (lying-down transitions) are roughly interchangeable in evidentiary weight; no strong literature or tracker signal picks among them.
Source: SisFall Table 2 (primary); SPARK docs/DATA_COLLECTION_PROTOCOL.md §4.2.
Confidence: Supported inference (D16/D17/D19 high-confidence; D11/D12 lower-confidence, presented as best-available default pending Aaradhya's call).
Relevance to SPARK: Aaradhya (protocol owner) should confirm/swap the last 2 ADL rows; everything else in this memo is ready to drop in as-is.

### Evidence table

| Finding | Evidence | Source | Confidence | SPARK implication |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SisFall taxonomy = 15 falls (F01–F15) + 19 ADLs (D01–D19), 38 subjects, 200Hz | Verbatim Table 1/2 from indexed primary-source PDF | Sucerquia et al. 2017, Sensors 17(1):198 | Established | Confirms doc's "15 Trials"/"19 Trials" headers are consistent with a real published taxonomy, not arbitrary |
| SPARK F01–F08/D01–D14 are reworded analogs, not SisFall copies | Row-by-row content diff | DATA_COLLECTION_PROTOCOL.md §4 vs. SisFall Table 1/2 | Established | Can't append SisFall's raw F09–F15/D15–D19 blindly; must map first to avoid duplicates |
| 7 unused SisFall fall types (F05,F09,F10,F12,F13,F14,F15) = 7 missing slots; F07 excluded on safety grounds | Mapping + SisFall's own stair-fall safety exclusion precedent | SisFall Table 1 methodology text; SPARK §2.1/§3 | Established (mapping) / Supported inference (F07 exclusion) | Clean, evidence-traceable F09–F15 fill, ready to insert |
| ADL gap: 7 unused SisFall types for 5 slots; D16/D17/D19 strong picks, D11/D12 judgment call | Mapping + SisFall's stated false-positive-similarity rationale for ADL selection | SisFall Table 2 methodology text; SPARK §4.2 | Supported inference | 3/5 D-rows are high-confidence; owner should confirm final 2 |

### Contradictions and limitations
- No contradiction in the SisFall taxonomy itself — single, stable, unrevised primary source since 2017 (14-year-old publicly cited dataset; taxonomy not part of any known errata).
- The F07 exclusion and the D11/D12 ADL picks are this researcher's inference, not something stated in the tracker or protocol doc — flagged explicitly above, not asserted as settled fact.
- SPARK's F04 ("backward fall while sitting, miss seat") and the proposed SisFall-derived rows do not overlap — double-checked to avoid the most likely duplication risk (SisFall F11, "backward fall trying to sit down," is already SPARK's F04, so F11 was correctly excluded from the new rows).
- This memo does not re-verify Track 8's separate elderly-vs-young-adult kinematics-validity question (§2.2 inclusion criteria) — out of this track's scope by the parent task's own division of labor.
- Draft rows are proposals for a human/orchestrator-approved follow-up edit; per task instructions no repo edit was made.

### Recommendation
1. Insert the 7 fall rows and 5 ADL rows below into §4.1/§4.2 of docs/DATA_COLLECTION_PROTOCOL.md (follow-up task, not this one).
2. Aaradhya should confirm: (a) no table prop is planned for fall simulations, validating the F07 exclusion; (b) the final 2 ADL rows (D11/D12 recommended, D13/D14 as alternates).
3. Feed Finding 2 (SPARK ≠ verbatim SisFall) back to whoever owns thesis Ch.4/5 methodology write-up, since "SisFall-compatible" (tracker v54, line 43) should be phrased as "taxonomy-complementary," not "identical," for accuracy.

**Draft rows — §4.1 Fall Simulation Trials (add after F08):**

| Code | Activity Description | Execution Instructions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **F09** | Forward fall while jogging (trip) | Jog 3–4 paces on approach at a reduced/controlled pace, simulate tripping on obstacle, fall forward onto hands/mat. |
| **F10** | Lateral fall when trying to get up | From seated position on chair, begin rising, lose lateral balance mid-rise, fall onto left/right flank onto adjacent mat. |
| **F11** | Forward fall when trying to sit down | Approach chair from front, misjudge seat position while lowering, pitch forward and fall onto hands/mat instead of sitting. |
| **F12** | Lateral fall when trying to sit down | Approach chair, lose lateral balance while lowering to seat, fall onto left/right flank onto mat beside chair. |
| **F13** | Forward fall while seated (fainting/drowsiness) | Seated in chair, simulate sudden fainting/falling asleep, pitch forward off chair onto mat. |
| **F14** | Backward fall while seated (fainting/drowsiness) | Seated in chair, simulate sudden fainting/falling asleep, fall backward off chair onto mat. |
| **F15** | Lateral fall while seated (fainting/drowsiness) | Seated in chair, simulate sudden fainting/falling asleep, fall to left/right side off chair onto mat. |

**Draft rows — §4.2 ADL Trials (add after D14):**

| Code | Activity Description | Duration / Repetitions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **D15** | Bending at the waist without bending knees (straight-leg forward bend), then standing | 5 repetitions |
| **D16** | Getting into a car/taxi, remaining seated briefly, then getting out | 5 repetitions |
| **D17** | Gentle jump without falling (e.g. reaching a high object) | 5 repetitions |
| **D18** | Sitting, attempting to rise, and collapsing back into the chair (near-fall, no actual fall) | 5 repetitions |
| **D19** | Lying down slowly onto a mat/bed, pausing, then sitting up again | 5 repetitions |

(Note: D15–D19 above are numbered sequentially per SPARK's own convention, not 1:1 to SisFall's D-numbers — mapped content is SisFall D16, D17, D19, D11, D12 respectively, in that order. D18 and D19 here are the lower-confidence judgment-call picks per Finding 4.)

### Sources
1. Sucerquia, A.; López, J.D.; Vargas-Bonilla, J.F. "SisFall: A Fall and Movement Dataset." Sensors 2017, 17(1), 198. DOI: 10.3390/s17010198. https://doi.org/10.3390/s17010198 (open access, MDPI). Primary source for full F01–F15/D01–D19 taxonomy, Table 1 & Table 2, p.4.
2. SPARK repo, github.com/AaradhyaDT/SPARK, main @ 53f194de7cd0679c866d905275b465f80c0d9bfb: docs/DATA_COLLECTION_PROTOCOL.md (§2.1, §3.2, §4.1, §4.2); dev_logs/SPARK_TRACKER.md v54 (line 43, Action #23 entries).
3. SPARK main NLM research notebook (2c00f5a4-98dc-4783-96d1-3682fa3cb516), source_id c4f5928e-20ca-4f11-9644-4d063ffc98f9 — already-indexed full text of source 1, used for verbatim table verification instead of re-adding a duplicate source.
